bib.title: The Power of Noise: Redefining Retrieval for RAG Systems
bib.venue: SIGIR '24 (47th International ACM SIGIR Conference), Washington, DC

question: What kinds of retrieved passages (relevant, distracting, random), in what number and position, make an LLM answer best in a RAG prompt, and are current retrievers ideal?
hypothesis: Implied: semantically close but non-answering (distracting) documents are not harmless, and the common assumption that only relevant context helps should be re-tested; the authors did not expect random noise to help.
contributions: First comprehensive study of the impact of the type of retrieved documents in RAG on LLM effectiveness.
Retrieval RAG heuristics that exploit the unexpected results.

method.summary: Prompts are built from the NQ-open gold passage plus controlled numbers and positions of distracting (top retrieved non-answer), random (Wikipedia, Reddit, or random-word) documents, and fed to four 4-bit quantised open LLMs with greedy decoding. Accuracy is whether any gold answer string is contained in the output. A second set of experiments uses real retrieval (Contriever or BM25 top-k) padded with random documents up to the context limit.
method.task: open-domain QA (NQ-open) with extractive answers of at most 5 tokens

datasets.name: NQ-open (Natural Questions open)
datasets.size: 72,209 train-set queries and 2,889 test-set queries; corpus of 21,035,236 documents
datasets.split: oracle experiments (Sections 5.1-5.3): 10K queries sampled from the train set; RAG-in-practice experiments (5.4): test set
datasets.source: English Wikipedia dump of 20 December 2018, split into non-overlapping 100-word passages as in DPR; NQ gold documents added to the corpus
datasets.preprocessing: Gold documents of NQ added to the Wikipedia set to avoid temporal mismatch; other answer-containing documents are not treated as gold

datasets.name: Reddit Webis-TLDR-17
datasets.source: Voelske et al. 2017, used as a source of random documents in a different style

datasets.name: Random-word nonsense sentences
datasets.source: made up of random words, used as random documents

models.name: MPT (instruct)
models.context: 2048 tokens (limit set by authors, same as pretraining)

models.name: Contriever
models.architecture: BERT-based dense retriever, unsupervised contrastive training; embedding = average of last-layer hidden states

models.name: ADORE
models.architecture: dense retriever trained with dynamic hard negatives

other.use: only to pick distracting docs in a 1/2/4 distractor check with Llama2

inference.samples: one greedy run per query; no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: Zero-shot, no few-shot exemplars. Instruction first, then documents (Document [id](Title: ...) text), then question, then Answer. Instruction and query always at start and end. Base and instruct versions tested; only instruct reported.
inference.retrieval: Top-k from Contriever (FAISS flat inner product) or BM25 over ~21M 100-word passages; random documents sampled uniformly from the corpus (or Reddit / random words) are added up to the context limit; k in 1-10 and up to 18 added docs

parameters.gold_position: far [I, gold, distract..., Q], mid [I, distract, gold, distract, Q], near [I, distract..., gold, Q]
parameters.distractors: counts 0,1,2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18 (read from Table 1 rows; >10 only for Llama2)

other.prompt_overflow: settings exceeding model input limit are excluded (shown as '-')

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: Binary: 1 if at least one of the predefined correct answers (NQ-open aliases) is contained in the LLM response, else 0; averaged over queries

metrics.name: Top-k accuracy of retriever
metrics.definition: Fraction of queries with the answer string present in the top-k retrieved documents

eval.protocol: Wilcoxon test against the base row; p<0.01 for Tables 1-4, p<0.05 for Table 5; asterisk marks non-significant cells. No seeds or confidence intervals.

availability.weights: public open models (not released by authors)

prompts.text: You are given a question and you MUST respond by EXTRACTING the answer (max 5 tokens) from one of the provided documents. If none of the documents contain the answer, respond with NO-RES.

evidence.quote: we adopt a greedy generation approach with a maximum response length of 15 tokens

results.claim: Adding random documents to the retrieved set until the context is full improves Llama2 accuracy by up to 0.07 (+35%) with 4 retrieved documents.
results.setup: NQ-open test, Llama2-7B, Contriever, [I, random, q, Q], 4 retrieved docs
results.quote: gains in terms of accuracy up to 0.07 (+35%) in the case of 4 retrieved documents

results.claim: In the oracle gold setting, random documents placed near the query raise MPT accuracy by 0.08 (+36%).
results.setup: gold + random documents, near position [I, random, gold, Q], MPT-7B
results.note: Text sentence continues 'the case of MPT'. Table 2 MPT near: 0.2148 gold-only vs 0.2930 with 4 random.

results.claim: Distracting documents degrade accuracy progressively, by more than 0.38 (-67%) in some cases.
results.setup: gold + distracting documents, four LLMs, far/mid/near
results.quote: with accuracy deteriorating by more than 0.38 (−67%)

results.claim: A single distracting document already causes a sharp drop, with peaks of 0.24 (-25%).
Llama2 gold-only accuracy is 0.5642 versus 0.1123 closed-book.
results.table: Table 1, row 0, column Llama2; closed-book 0.1123 in caption

results.claim: With ADORE (hard-negative-trained retriever) selecting distractors, Llama2 accuracy with 1, 2 and 4 distractors is 0.4068, 0.3815, 0.3626, lower than the no-distractor 0.5642 and lower than Contriever distractors.
results.quote: we obtain an accuracy of 0.4068, 0.3815, and 0.3626

results.note: Table 1 values for 18 distractors: near 0.3781, far 0.2348, mid 0.1795.

results.claim: Adding BM25-retrieved context plus random documents gives an average accuracy increase of 3-4 percentage points.
results.quote: an average increase in accuracy of 3-4 percentage points

results.claim: BM25 has higher top-k answer-containing accuracy than Contriever (k=1,2,4,10).
results.setup: NQ-open test set, answer-string presence in top-k
results.note: Authors admit answer-string match may overstate relevance.

results.setup: Llama2-7B, Contriever, Reddit Webis-TLDR-17 random docs

results.claim: Even random-word nonsense documents improve accuracy over the Wikipedia-random base case.
results.quote: Remarkably, even in this scenario, we observe a performance

results.claim: Falcon does not improve with random docs in the oracle gold setting but does with retrieved docs plus random Reddit docs.
results.note: Gains are small: e.g. 5 retrieved 0.1942 -> 0.2118 with 3 random; many cells not significant.

results.claim: Best configuration: retrieve a small set (3 to 5 documents) and pad with random documents up to the context limit.

results.claim: Attention entropy rises about 3X when random documents are added to the gold-only prompt; offered as a hypothesis not a confirmed explanation.
results.setup: gold-only vs [I, random, gold, Q], model not specified in the sentence (Llama2 used for attention figure)
results.quote: the entropy of the systems has a 3X increase
results.note: Authors say they cannot answer the question definitively.

limits: Authors concede no formal theory explains why random documents help; the attention-entropy account is a hint only (Section 5.5).
Accuracy is substring containment of NQ answer aliases; 'Roosevelt' vs 'President Roosevelt' is scored wrong, and authors leave better answer-variant analysis to future work (Section 4.6).
Only NQ-open (Wikipedia), extractive answers up to 5 tokens, zero-shot prompts; few-shot is out of scope.
Models are 2.7B-7B and 4-bit quantised, context 2048-4096; behaviour of larger or long-context models is not tested.
Oracle experiments use a 10K-query sample of the train set; no seeds, repeats or confidence intervals beyond Wilcoxon tests.
Falcon does not show the random-document gain in the oracle gold setting; Falcon and Llama2 do not consistently show lost-in-the-middle.

Gains from random docs shrink or vanish with BM25 relative to Contriever in some cells because BM25 retrieves answer-containing docs more often; top-k accuracy via answer-string match may overstate relevance.
Gains are with 'correct positioning' (random docs placed far from query, gold/retrieved docs near query); random docs near the query as in far/mid hurt Llama2 and Phi-2.
Later work (not in this paper) may have dated the specific models used.

terms.definition: the original context in the NQ dataset, the passage of a Wikipedia page containing the answer
passages that, akin to the gold document, contain the correct answer and are contextually useful; the gold document is a relevant document
semantically similar to the query but do not contain the correct answer; in practice the top-scoring retrieved documents that are not relevant
neither related to the query nor contain the answer; randomly sampled from the corpus
gold document position relative to the query: adjacent, middle of context, or as far as possible
